protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: Confirmed. At reported commit 1802525be27d33e19a9a83c163e331a1d13b1892, ReceiveTcpMsg() drains an oversized TCP encapsulation body but returns the attacker-declared body length plus the 24-byte header. HandleDataOnTcpSocket() then creates BufReader(s_buf, num_read) although s_buf is only 1800 bytes; the forged logical limit lets SendRRData CPF parsing read beyond s_buf. The vendor issue records the ASan global-buffer-overflow and was closed completed.

The exact diff changes the oversized branch from returning disposeOfLargePacket() (0 on a fully drained body) to returning remaining + ENCAPSULATION_HEADER_LENGTH after a successful drain. git log -S finds only this introduction and the later direct fix; 90721b00e44e461d14501bb20714a4d71d9e18e4 introduced the drain path but still returned 0 and is not the BIC.
